page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 16 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor, operating at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core and multi-core capabilities, with Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores placing in the top 25 percent. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, which assist in vector calculations and cryptography tasks, as evidenced by strong performance in Passmark CPU encryption tests. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and image processing benchmarks also rank in the top tier. Conversely, multi-core stress-ng performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations fall within the average range.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides a high density of dedicated compute resources relative to its memory footprint, making it a viable option for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive memory allocations or local NVMe storage. The lack of bundled local storage means storage requirements must be met via network-attached volumes. This instance is suited for workloads such as multi-threaded decompression, text and image processing, web serving, and general compute-intensive applications.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of memory, powered by an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor running at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Operating under the KVM hypervisor, this instance provides a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and lacks local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark data shows strong single-core and multi-core performance, particularly in cryptography, text processing, and multi-threaded decompression, while memory bandwidth and database operations perform at average levels. The instance is qualitatively cost-effective for compute-heavy tasks that do not demand high memory density or local storage. It is suited for web serving, image processing, and multi-threaded data decompression workloads.
